```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(icesASD)
```

The catch scenarios table of an ICES advice sheet is uploaded to the
Advice and Scenarios Database as an XML file at <https://asd.ices.dk>.
The XML file is usually made with the ICES catch scenarios Excel template;
this vignette shows how to make the same file in R with **icesASD**.

The example is the 2026 advice for greater silver smelt (*Argentina silus*)
in divisions 5.b and 6.a (`aru.27.5b6a`).

The file is built from five pieces:

| Piece | Function | Excel template |
|---|---|---|
| Stock information | `asdInfo()` | top of the *Catch Scenarios* sheet |
| Column headers | `asdColumns()` | table headers, year and units rows |
| Row headers | `asdRows()` | basis and scenario labels |
| Values | a data frame | the body of the table |
| Footnotes | `asdNotes()` | the *Catch Scenario Notes* sheet |

## The catch scenarios table

The table for this stock is included in the package as a CSV file, laid out
as it appears in the advice sheet: the purpose, basis and label of each
scenario, followed by one column per variable.

```{r read}
tab <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "aru.27.5b6a_2026_catch_scenarios.csv", package = "icesASD"),
  check.names = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8"
)
tab[, c("purpose", "label", "Total catch", "F 6–14")]
```

## Stock information

```{r info}
info <- asdInfo(
  stockCode = "aru.27.5b6a",
  AssessmentYear = 2026,
  contact = "Assessor Name"
)
```

The purpose is always `"Advice"`, as in the Excel template.

## Column headers

Each column has a label, the year it refers to and a unit. Units are ICES
[MUNIT](https://vocab.ices.dk/?ref=155) codes such as `t`, `ratio` and `%`.
For % change columns, the year is the last year of the comparison.
Footnote symbols are part of the label.

```{r columns}
columns <- asdColumns(
  label = names(tab)[-(1:3)],
  year = c(2027, 2027, 2027, 2027, 2027, 2027, 2028, 2028, 2027, 2027, 2028),
  unit = c("t", "t", "t", "ratio", "ratio", "ratio", "t", "%", "%", "%", "%")
)
columns
```

The data frame uses the element names of the XML file. The column IDs
(`AK_ID`) are the column numbers of the Excel template, where the table starts
in column E (5). Up to 50 columns are allowed.

The type of each column can optionally be given in `type`,
using codes from the ICES [StockDataType](https://vocab.ices.dk/?ref=1528)
vocabulary (`Catch`, `FishingPressure`, `StockSize`, ...). It is left out of
the file when not given.

## Row headers

Each scenario has a label, a basis and a purpose. Up to three rows can be the
basis of the advice (`"BasisAdvice"`); the others are `"OtherScenarios"`.
The basis is a code from the ICES
[CatchScenariosBasis](https://vocab.ices.dk/?ref=1570) vocabulary
(`MSY`, `MP`, `PA`, `FMSYranges`, `NoAdv`, `Other`); empty entries become
`"Other"`.

```{r rows}
rows <- asdRows(
  label = tab$label,
  basis = tab$basis,
  purpose = tab$purpose
)
rows[c("AR_ID", "CS_Purpose", "CS_Basis")]
```

The row IDs (`AR_ID`) are the template's row numbers: rows 12 to 14 are the
basis of the advice and the other scenarios start at row 16.

## Values

The values are the body of the table, with one row per scenario and one
column per column header, in the same order:

```{r values}
values <- tab[-(1:3)]
```

Empty cells are left out of the file. Values can be numbers or text, for
example `"<1"`.

## Footnotes

```{r notes}
notes <- asdNotes(
  symbol = c("*", "**", "***", "^", "^^", "^^^"),
  note = c(
    "ICES cannot estimate projected landings and discards.",
    "SSB 2028 relative to SSB 2027 (96 380 tonnes).",
    "The percent change in TAC is not presented because the advice area and TAC unit do not match.",
    "Advice value for 2027 relative to advice value for 2026 (18 441 tonnes).",
    paste(
      "This probability relates to the short-term probability of SSB < Blim and is not",
      "comparable to the long-term probability of SSB < Blim tested in simulations when",
      "estimating fishing mortality reference points."
    ),
    "These reference points have not been estimated for this stock."
  )
)
```

Text such as `<` can be written as it is; it is escaped correctly in the file.

## Checking and writing the file

`writeASDxml()` checks the table and writes the file, named
`<stockCode>_<AssessmentYear>_catch_scenarios.xml` by default:

```{r write, eval = FALSE}
writeASDxml(info, columns, rows, values, notes)
```

The checks (also available on their own as `checkASD()`) compare codes
against the ICES vocabularies, which needs an internet connection, check the
layout of the table against the limits of the Excel template, and check that
the footnote symbols used in the labels match the notes. Errors stop the file
being written; warnings are reported.

For this table the checks find two notes that are not used in any label:

```
Warning message:
  note '***' is not used in any label
  note '^^^' is not used in any label
```

The checks can be skipped with `check = FALSE`, for example if the vocabulary
server cannot be reached.

## The file

```{r show, echo = FALSE}
file <- writeASDxml(info, columns, rows, values, notes,
                    file = tempfile(fileext = ".xml"), check = FALSE)
xml <- readLines(file, encoding = "UTF-8")
```

The file starts with the stock information and the column headers:

```{r head, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
cat(xml[1:(grep("<Scenarios_Columns>", xml)[3] - 1)], sep = "\n")
```

followed by the row headers, one `Scenarios_Values` record per filled cell
of the table, and the footnotes:

```{r tail, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
last <- max(grep("<Scenarios_Values>", xml))
cat(xml[last:length(xml)], sep = "\n")
```

## Uploading

Upload the file at <https://asd.ices.dk>.
